title: Joins and grain
summary: A synthetic SQL example for checking code, tables and explanatory blocks.

blocks.text: State the grain of each table before joining. One-to-many joins can multiply rows.

blocks.title: Aggregate lines before joining
blocks.code:
WITH line_totals AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS line_amount
  FROM order_lines
  GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, l.line_amount
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN line_totals l USING (order_id);

blocks.question: What should you check after a join?
blocks.answer: Check row counts, key uniqueness at the intended grain, unmatched keys and aggregate reconciliation.
